articles.title: "Virtually Catatonic": 49ers Legend Steve Young Needed an IV Drip After Vomiting From Drinking Following Historic Super Bowl Win
articles.summary: Who would have thought that a night of celebration win would turn into a medical emergency for Steve Young? On January 29, 1995, Steve Young finally got his...
articles.body:
Who would have thought that a night of celebration win would turn into a medical emergency for Steve Young?

On January 29, 1995, Steve Young finally got his chance to shine on football's biggest stage. Young put on a show in Super Bowl XXIX, throwing a record six touchdown passes, leading the San Francisco 49ers to a 49-26 win over the San Diego Chargers.

After the game ended, Young headed for the interviews, where he spent a long time. It was also uncomfortably hot that night. Veteran Peter King, in an appearance on 25 Whistles and who was working for Sports Illustrated at the time, recalled that Young had asked if he could get something to drink. King got him three Gatorades, which Young drank in minutes.

"By the time we got in the car to go back to his hotel, he pukes a red torrent of puke all over the back of this limo," King said. "When we got back to the hotel, he had like a junior suite … And he was so dehydrated, he was virtually catatonic. The Miami-Dade Fire Rescue came up into his room, and they didn't put one IV of saline in him; they put two IV in him."

Per Sports Illustrated, Young's agent at the time, Leigh Steinberg recalled Young lying on the bed with his arms outstretched, "like a death-bed scene," resembling "the last supper or something."

However, according to King, the quarterback was still entertaining those who came to talk with him, including former teammates from BYU. Young, even in that state, was still able to bask in the happiness of his performance.

"At one point, he just looks up and he goes, 'What an unbelievable day.' He said, 'I never threw six touchdown passes as a kid in Connecticut. I never threw six in high school. Never threw six in college. Never threw six obviously in the NFL. And I did it in the biggest game of my life. How incredible is that?'

"He was just, even though he was weak as a kitten at that time, he was just so happy. As happy as I've ever seen a human being after winning the Super Bowl."

Young had reason to be jubilant. Once an afterthought for the 49ers during the time Joe Montana led the charge, Young proved doubters wrong with this Super Bowl victory.

He put up solid numbers on the field too. Steve Young completed 24 of 36 passes for 325 yards and six touchdowns without throwing an interception. He and the 49ers continued their legacy of being a Super Bowl contender even in Montana's absence. The Super Bowl XXIX was the only one that Young won as a starter; the other two he had won at San Francisco were as a backup to Montana.

However, even with two IV lines pumping saline into him, Young had a clear mind. Someone in the room said, "Joe, who?" to which Young took offense.

"No, don't do that!" he replied. "Joe's a good guy."

Per SI, King was with Steve until 3 am, and he later wrote up his assignment.

"It was less a file and more like a complete story—he estimates 1,500 to 2,000 words long; [Michael] Silver guesses more like 3,000—with a scene opener, dialogue and a ton of details, topped by the symbolic moment of an exhausted Super Bowl MVP purging himself. It was, King knew, journalistic gold," Chris Ballard wrote for Sports Illustrated.

articles.title: Drake Maye’s biggest supporter is Ann Michael, and her journey from UNC graduate to Patriots fan favorite is worth knowing
articles.summary: Ann Michael Maye has spent more than a decade beside Drake Maye, and New England now knows her almost as well as it knows him.
articles.body: Ann Michael Maye has spent more than a decade beside Drake Maye, and New England now knows her almost as well as it knows him. The Patriots quarterback met her in middle school, followed her to the same college and married her in June 2025. She earned her UNC business degree that May and then moved to Boston to build a life around his NFL career. Fans noticed quickly. Between her viral baking videos and a hoodie she wore to a playoff game, she has become one of the team's most recognised faces off the field.Who is Ann Michael Maye, Drake Maye's biggest supporter?Ann Michael Hudson was born on August 11, 2003, in Huntersville, North Carolina, and grew up around football. Her father played at Wofford College. Her younger brother, Tad, was one of Drake's backup quarterbacks at UNC in 2023 before he moved to Coastal Carolina.She and Drake started dating at 12. Both went to William A. Hough High School in Cornelius, and they made the relationship Instagram-official in January 2020. After graduation, both chose Chapel Hill.Her own résumé is strong. She earned a business degree from UNC's Kenan-Flagler Business School in 2025, with minors in entrepreneurship and conflict management. She served as vice president of finance in her sorority and held an internship at Deloitte Consulting. She finished at 21, a year behind Drake in age but right alongside him in ambition. She was also with Drake on draft night in 2024, when New England took him third overall, and after college she left North Carolina, the only home she had known, to live near him in Boston.Drake proposed in January 2025, soon after his rookie season ended. The wedding followed on June 21 at Grandfather Golf and Country Club in Linville.How did Ann Michael Maye become a Patriots fan favorite?It started with food. Her Bakemas videos went viral, and by January she said she had finished filming a baking show of her own. Her TikTok comments fill up with Patriots fans, and some now call her the first lady of New England. A football household likely helped too. Growing up with a father and brother who played the game, she already knew how a long season feels.She also shows up. Before the Divisional Round game against the Texans, she arrived at Gillette Stadium in an "I Heart Drake Maye" sweatshirt, the same design many fans had been wearing. She has also joined Dave Portnoy for a pizza review in Needham.Calling her the biggest supporter is fair, but she does not hold that role alone. After the Wild Card win over the Chargers, Drake talked about his parents and brothers first, then added, "And obviously, Ann Michael, so I can't forget about her." His parents, Mark and Aimee, are at every game too.What sets her apart is the timing. She made the move to Boston before the Super Bowl run made it look smart.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce's 1.7 billion franchise gets major boost after Guardians' dramatic ALDS comeback
articles.summary: Travis Kelce had plenty to celebrate as the Cleveland Guardians completed a remarkable comeback in the American League Division Series.
articles.body: Travis Kelce had plenty to celebrate as the Cleveland Guardians completed a remarkable comeback in the American League Division Series. The Kansas City Chiefs star watched from the stands as Cleveland defeated the Chicago White Sox 2-0 in Game 5 on October 10, sealing a series victory after losing the opening two games. Now a minority owner of the Guardians, Kelce shared his excitement after witnessing the team fight its way into the American League Championship Series. His message was clear: he believes Cleveland has plenty left to accomplish this postseason.Travis Kelce backs the Guardians after their ALDS triumphCleveland's comeback gave Kelce another reason to show his support for his hometown team. After the Guardians fell behind in the series, they won three consecutive games to eliminate Chicago and keep their championship hopes alive.Speaking after the decisive victory, Kelce made his confidence in the team clear."The ALCS is ours baby, I can feel it," he said.He also spoke about the atmosphere surrounding the franchise and the excitement building among Cleveland fans."The energy in Cleveland is electric right now," he said. "Shout out to everybody. Go Guards, baby, Go Guards!"Kelce's enthusiasm reflects his growing connection to the Guardians beyond his role as a fan. The NFL tight end became a minority owner of the franchise earlier this season, adding another chapter to his long-standing relationship with Cleveland.The city has remained an important part of his identity despite his success with the Chiefs. Kelce has repeatedly credited his hometown for helping shape his life and career."I say it all the time: I’m a kid from the Heights living the dream," he said. "I credit every good thing in my life to Cleveland.”Guardians prepare for ALCS after José Ramírez and Gavin Williams deliverThe Guardians backed up Kelce's confidence with a strong finish to the ALDS. José Ramírez played a key role in the turnaround, recording two home runs and seven RBIs across the series. His two-run homer off Sean Burke proved decisive in Game 5, helping Cleveland secure the 2-0 victory.Kelce described the experience as a special moment in his life.“It was [more than a moment money could buy],” Kelce said in an article done by MLB.com, “one of the coolest moments of my life.”Cleveland's pitching staff also helped turn the series around. The team allowed just 10 runs across the final three games, while its 21-strikeout performance in Game 5 set a postseason record for a nine-inning game. The Guardians also recorded 19 strikeouts in Game 3, giving them the two highest totals in that category for a nine-inning postseason contest.Kelce also praised the bond among the players, highlighting the unity that helped Cleveland recover from its early setbacks.“This team has camaraderie,” Kelce continued Saturday night. “You can see how much energy they have for each other, how much love they have for each other. And that’s hard to beat..."The Guardians now turn their attention to the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays, with Game 1 scheduled for October 12. Cleveland will look to carry its momentum into the next round as it pursues a place in the World Series.For Kelce, the excitement is about more than a single win. His hometown team has given him another reason to believe, and he will be hoping the Guardians can keep their postseason run alive.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Winners and losers as Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans: 'I was praying something happened'
articles.summary: "I don't even know if I'm allowed to say [but] I was praying something happened with him," Garrett Wilson told Yahoo Sports after the Jets beat the Browns. "...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — In the New York Jets' postgame locker room on Sunday afternoon, Garrett Wilson lit up.

The former Ohio State receiver who became a top-10 pick in the NFL Draft was hearing the latest news of another former Ohio State receiver who became a top-10 pick in the draft.

And Wilson, who overlapped with Harrison for one season in Columbus, was thrilled to hear the Arizona Cardinals were trading Harrison to the Houston Texans .

"I don't even know if I'm allowed to say [but] I was praying something happened with him," Wilson told Yahoo Sports after the Jets beat the Browns . "The fact he did, and it's a spot like Houston? Man, I'm happy for him."

Who else is happy for the highly-touted prospect that didn't take off in two-plus Arizona seasons? And who might be disappointed that the Cardinals are dealing Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for 2027 second- and sixth-round picks?

Based on conversations with players and execs around the league, here are Yahoo Sports' winners and losers of the trade:

Cardinals' arsenal to rebuild: It was hardly a secret across the league that the Cardinals wanted a second-round draft pick and change in exchange for their physically gifted wideout. But multiple teams I spoke with in recent weeks were not convinced Harrison warranted that cost. One NFC talent evaluator told me last week they thought there was "zero chance" Harrison was worth a second- or third-round pick. A high-ranking AFC executive told me that for a Day 3 pick — that is, fourth round or later — the value would be worth pursuing Harrison, but no higher.

The Cardinals capitalized on a desperate Texans team that had reason to believe in Harrison more than 31 counterparts. And thus two seasons and four games after selecting Harrison fourth overall, the Cardinals not only get a second-round pick but they get a second-round pick in the talent-rich 2027 draft even amid trends to trade high 2028 picks (hi, Baltimore Ravens for Cam Jurgens and New England Patriots for A.J. Brown) to save up for the expected treasure trove in April.

C.J. Stroud: With Stroud at Ohio State in 2022, Harrison posted a whopping 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns in 13 games. The duo connected on three touchdowns in the Rose Bowl alone that season. Teammates from their time speak to the on-field chemistry quarterback and receiver built quickly, the work ethic that had them in the building early and the cerebral nature that helped them connect.

Stroud has played better this season than his team's 1-4 record suggests, completing 64.3% of his passes for 1,402 yards, six touchdowns and no interceptions in five games. He's rushed for another 71 yards and a score. But the Texans' receiving corps has proven incredibly shallow. Tank Dell has yet to return from injured reserve after knee surgery following a December dislocation of his kneecap and multiple torn ligaments. Jayden Higgins suffered a season-ending ACL tear during training camp. Nico Collins missed Weeks 2 and 3 with a hamstring strain suffered in practice. What can Harrison add? "They don't really miss now together," Wilson said. "C.J. don't miss much anyway, but when he got a guy like that, that got a catch radius like that, runs good routes? It's going to be fun to watch."

Marvin Harrison Jr.'s career: This trade is likely only a reality because of how much Harrison struggled in Arizona. A combination of 2025 health setbacks (concussion, appendicitis, two heel injuries) and target plummet this year meant he finishes his Cardinals tenure with 108 catches for 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns in 33 games (30 starts). This season, Harrison had just 13 targets across four games; he caught five for 85 yards and a score. The high-ranking AFC executive believed Houston could ignite something in Harrison for reasons beyond the college reunion: the benefit of the excitement tends to follow a new trade acquisition, as opposed to the disappointment surrounding a high-draft pick that doesn't quickly materialize. Another AFC executive believed that even Harrison's up-and-down tenure in Arizona showed his speed, quickness and agility at the pro level. Turn those flashes into marks of consistency, and Texans fans have reason to be excited.

"I know the belief system that he's going to have around him in the Texans," Wilson said. "I know what he can do. So for me, it's just a ticking-time bomb with him. I can't wait to watch him erupt. He's got all the ability in the world and now he's playing with someone that he's been with before. They got great chemistry. And I saw it from Day 1 at O State. I can't wait to watch. You got me excited."

The chance the Texans defy history again: Since 1979, only seven times in NFL history has a team started 0-3 and advanced to the playoffs, per NBC Sports . The Texans claim two of those seven, most recently rebounding last year from 0-3 to 12-5. The Texans proved they belonged in the playoffs when they beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh, 30-6, in the wild-card round. The Patriots then outlasted the Texans 28-16 in the divisional round. Could the Texans rebound from 0-4 to make the playoffs? Only one team, the 1992 Chargers, have accomplished that feat. With 17 chances instead of 16, the Texans, now 1-4, have one more chance to showcase their upgraded roster than that Chargers team. Will it be enough?

The cost of desperation: The Texans needed to do something . Head coach DeMeco Ryans already stripped defensive coordinator Matt Burke of play-calling this past week . Pair that with an 0-4 start and a need to make a contract decision on Stroud soon, and Houston let Arizona squeeze more out of the deal than less-frenzied franchises would have copped. If the Texans advance deep into the playoffs, perhaps this pays off. But it's worth remembering that the Texans' defense has still regressed meaningfully from last year. Holding the winless Titans to three points in Sunday's victory is better than a loss, but the Titans have been held to 10 or fewer points in three of five games this year so it's not sufficient to prove the group is settling. What will it take for Harrison, whose fifth-year option decision looms in May, to justify the sacrifice of a more cost-controlled 2027 second-round pick in a talent-rich draft? If Harrison approaches his draft billing, it will be worth it. But two-plus seasons and several injuries in, as he scrambles to pick up a new offense midseason, how likely is that?

The 'film means everything' crowd: It's disingenuous to criticize Harrison's college career and the film that propelled him to the fourth overall pick. Harrison's 2,613 yards and 31 touchdowns, including two seasons in which he surpassed 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns. He showed he could thrive with Stroud, and he showed he could thrive with quarterback Kyle McCord. So the Cardinals were comfortable spending big on him despite Harrison's decision to not participate in scouting combine drills. Two-and-a-half years later, some talent evaluators wonder how significant that decision was. While an AFC executive argued for the importance of production on the field rather than in the vacuum of test-like combine settings, talent evaluators from two NFC teams wondered if Harrison was "overdrafted" relative to his career thus far in part because of missing information about his physical traits compared to historical precedent.

"The perception was that he was fast and strong and explosive and all that, but now you question whether the testing [would have] come back a little bit underwhelming," one NFC evaluator told Yahoo Sports, "and then if it would have come back underwhelming, he wouldn't have been [drafted] as high."

NFC teams outside the NFC West: The NFC West sent three teams to the playoffs last season: the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. All three won at least one playoff game, the NFC championship staged between the Rams and Seahawks before Seattle beat the Patriots for the Lombardi Trophy. The Rams entered this season with overwhelming Super Bowl odds, and the Niners and Seahawks started hotter than their Los Angeles foe through four weeks. The Cardinals were already going to be the weak link in the division, but with Harrison, the chance of the any-given-Sunday in-division upset drops further. And the chance of the NFC West's other three teams taking home two wins a pop vs. the Cardinals, helping them win not only a division berth but one to two wild-card berths, increases.

Cardinals' current offensive players: Few expected Arizona to win many games this season amid a rebuild, a hole in the quarterback room and what seemed to be an unforgiving schedule this year. With the Cardinals falling to 1-4 after this Sunday, that expectation might not change. But the offense's chance to function in head coach Mike LaFleur's first season does dip with the loss of Harrison. Even as Harrison commanded a lesser target share this season, the defensive attention he directed away from teammates was valuable. Harrison was on the field on 74% of offensive snaps through the Cardinals' first four games. That helped players like Michael Wilson and Trey McBride find creases in defenses, and it helped teammates like Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier face less-stacked boxes. By 2027 and afterward, perhaps the draft capital, a longer-term quarterback solution than Jacoby Brissett and more time in LaFleur's system will pay off. But 2026 looks bleaker for Arizona than it did last week.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo breathed a 'sigh of relief' after Commanders disaster overshadowed his fumble that squandered a chance for Giants win
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo kind of got bailed out by Commanders miscues. At least, for Skattebo, the bulk of the attention got shifted to Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn.
articles.body:
Before there was Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn frittering away an almost certain win there was Cam Skattebo.

The New York Giants were at Washington's 24-yard line Sunday with the game tied at 27 in need of only a field goal to secure a walkoff win in overtime. Rather than settle for a 41-yard kick, they ran the ball with Skattebo on first-and-10 in hope of getting into the end zone or, more likely, setting up Dominic Zvada for a shorter kick.

Neither happened. Instead, Skattebo fumbled, and the Commanders recovered. And what just seconds earlier looked like a Giants win turned into disaster for New York.

The Commanders instead had the ball with 1:55 remaining and a chance to drive for their own game-winning field-goal attempt.

They got into position to do so, and then they did this.

That's Daniels inexplicably running and getting tackled inbounds in field-goal range in the game's final seconds with no timeout.

And that's Quinn slamming his headset in frustration as the clock ticked down to zero on a 27-27 tie, his team having just squandered a chance at a win.

As for Skattebo, he was left off the hook by the play. Kind of.

Skattebo still fumbled away a likely Giants win. But instead of a loss, the Giants were gifted a tie. And the focus was taken off his late-game snafu and placed squarely on Daniels and Quinn instead.

For Skattebo, the moment added up to a "sigh of relief." But he recognized that he's not completely off the hook.

"It was a sigh of relief, you know," Skattebo told reporters at his locker. "I probably won't get reamed as much, but I'm still gonna get reamed. At the end of the day, my number was called, and I gave the ball up.

"If that happens again this year, I promise you that won't happen."

That's obviously not a promise Skattebo can guarantee to keep.

As for Sunday, Skattebo is content to not be the focus of the storyline on a Giants loss.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' 15 and the Mahomies foundation made a heartwarming announcement benefiting over 300 families
articles.summary: Last year, as Patrick Mahomes prepared for a rare Thanksgiving Day appearance with the Kansas City Chiefs, his charitable foundation brought a different
articles.body: Last year, as Patrick Mahomes prepared for a rare Thanksgiving Day appearance with the Kansas City Chiefs, his charitable foundation brought a different kind of victory to families across the community. The 15 and the Mahomies Foundation joined forces with Shelter KC to provide food to households facing hardship during the holiday season. The initiative reached more than 300 families, offering practical support at a time when many people face added pressure to put meals on the table. The announcement highlighted Mahomes' commitment to giving back beyond football and making a difference in the lives of those who need help.Patrick Mahomes' foundation supports more than 300 families during ThanksgivingThe 15 and the Mahomies Foundation shared details of its annual Family Feast, which brought volunteers and community partners together to help families prepare for Thanksgiving.“This Thanksgiving week, Shelter KC and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation hosted our annual Family Feast! With the help of some amazing volunteers, we were able to provide over 300 food bags to families in need. A huge THANK YOU to our volunteers and partners for making a difference this holiday season,” the foundation posted.The effort focused on a simple but important goal: helping families access food during a holiday often centred on sharing meals with loved ones. By distributing more than 300 food bags, the organisations offered direct assistance to households that might otherwise struggle to meet their needs.The announcement also recognised the volunteers and partners whose work helped make the event possible. Community programmes often depend on these contributions to reach people who need support, especially during busy holiday periods.Mahomes established the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019. The organisation works to support children and backs initiatives related to health, wellness, communities with limited resources and other charitable causes.The Thanksgiving event reflects how the foundation uses its platform to support people outside the sporting world. While Mahomes is best known for his achievements as the Chiefs' quarterback, projects like the Family Feast show another side of his public work.Patrick Mahomes balances Chiefs' playoff push with community workThe announcement came as Mahomes and the Chiefs entered a crucial stretch of their 2025 season. Kansas City had improved to a 6-5 record after defeating the Indianapolis Colts 23-20 in overtime, keeping its hopes of reaching the playoffs alive.The team was also preparing to face the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. It was a notable occasion for Kansas City, which had not played on Thanksgiving since beating the Denver Broncos in 2006.Despite the attention surrounding the holiday matchup, the foundation's announcement put the focus on families rather than football. The initiative also echoed similar charitable efforts by other major sports figures, including LeBron James, whose foundation helped provide food and turkeys to families in Akron, Ohio.For Mahomes, the Family Feast offered a reminder that community impact can extend well beyond the field. articles.title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs surpasses Barry Sanders for most NFL touchdowns scored before age 25
articles.summary: Gibbs could put that record far out of reach, not turning 25 until next March with 12 games remaining this season.
articles.body:
With two touchdowns in the Detroit Lions' 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, Jahmyr Gibbs surpassed Hall of Famer Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored before age 25 in his NFL career.

Gibbs had 56 TDs coming into Sunday's game, one behind Sanders on that particular list . He doesn't turn 25 until next March and the Lions had 13 games remaining on their 2026-27 schedule. So the fourth-year star had plenty of time to overtake the Lions legend.

The first of Gibbs' scores came on a 1-yard run early in the second quarter. That finished off a seven-play, 54-yard drive that tied the score at 7 after Detroit punted on its previous four possessions.

Gibbs overtook Sanders for the top spot in the fourth quarter. The Lions were already ahead 38-14 when he rushed on a play designed to go left. Faced with a wall of Arizona defenders, Gibbs changed direction — the type of play that invites some comparisons to Sanders — and dashed to the right, outrunning everyone to the right corner of the end zone.

The box score says Gibbs' TD was a 3-yard run, but he covered far more ground than that. It was another example of how much difficulty the Cardinals had trying to corral the Lions' star running back throughout the game.

In addition to his two TDs, Gibbs finished with 151 yards rushing on 25 carries. He added 56 yards receiving on five catches, compiling over 200 yards from scrimmage against an Arizona defense that ranked 23rd in the NFL with 1,405 yards allowed (and 20th with 470 rushing yards).

Five games into an already impressive career, Gibbs has recorded 46 rushing touchdowns and 12 receiving scores. He has 4,044 rushing yards and 581 yards receiving, emerging as the dual threat out of the backfield that the Lions envisioned when they selected him No. 12 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft.

Following Sunday's performance, Gibbs ranks second in the NFL with 504 rushing yards and is tied for the league lead with seven touchdowns.

Draft observers and Lions fans may remember that Gibbs' selection wasn't viewed favorably at the time. The perception across the NFL and those who cover it was that running backs were no longer impact players worth a high draft pick. Additionally, Detroit had signed free-agent running back David Montgomery, presumably to be the featured player at that position.

Four years later, no one is questioning the Lions for drafting Gibbs with a top-15 selection, nor for making him the highest-paid running back in the league with a three-year, $67.5 million contract extension during training camp this year.

One question that remains through the remainder of the 2026-27 season is how much distance Gibbs will put between him and Sanders — and other NFL greats including Randy Moss, Emmitt Smith and Jim Brown. If he follows his career averages of 14 rushing TDs and four receiving scores per season, Gibbs may put that record far out of reach.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 5: Another Sirianni mistake, plus Giants and Commanders both blowing a win
articles.summary: The Eagles blew the game prior to the final kickoff, and somehow both the Giants and Commanders blew overtime.
articles.body:
Bad news, Eagles fans: Your coach is back in the "momentous plays" list, and not in a good way.

For a second straight week, Nick Sirianni and the Eagles found themselves on the wrong end of a game they absolutely should have won.

In Week 4, it was coughing up a 10-point lead at home to the Rams. On Sunday, it was kicking off with a lead and eight seconds remaining … and somehow losing to the Jaguars in London.

Keeping it in the NFC East, we also had a game where both teams arguably coughed up a "sure" win in overtime . It's perhaps only fitting that there were zero NFC East victories in Week 5, even with two division teams going head to head.

We also scoured well beyond the NFC East to find Week 5's most momentous plays that shifted the tide in games dramatically.

1. The Eagles actually lost prior to kicking off inbounds

Yes, you absolutely can question why Nick Sirianni kicked inbounds to a team with no timeouts after taking the lead with just eight seconds left . It's fair criticism, and it cost the Eagles the game in the end.

But the way they mismanaged the clock prior to that point can't be dismissed. They had a chance to end it before the ensuing kickoff.

On second-and-10 from the Jacksonville 34-yard line with 21 seconds remaining and the Jaguars leading, 16-14, the Eagles threw a quick out to rookie Makai Lemon. It was a good play-call, netting 7 yards and improving the field position for the go-ahead field goal Jake Elliott would eventually make.

But there was too much time on the clock, and Lemon ran out of bounds after his catch, stopping the clock with 17 seconds left. Had Lemon just caught the ball and fallen down inbounds, the Jaguars would have been forced to call their final timeout around that same time, or perhaps a second or two fewer.

On third down, the Eagles could have run the ball and called timeout with just a few seconds left. That would have made Elliott's kick the final play of the game, win or lose. Then there's no kickoff to worry about.

The worst part is that the Jaguars called timeout before first down after the Eagles hit a big play to enter field-goal territory. (And they even did a favor to Philly, letting 20 seconds tick off the clock before burning it.) That should have been ample time for Siranni to instruct his players how to handle a catch and that they should not go out of bounds.

Instead, with the clock stopped after Lemon's catch, the Jaguars used their final timeout after Dameon Pierce's third-down carry. There were only eight seconds left when Elliott kicked off to the Jaguars, but those took a virtual eternity to tick off while Ameer Abdullah was running back the kickoff that set up Cam Little's miracle game-winner.

Every call Jaguars head coach Liam Coen made Sunday seemed to backfire, and yet one simple play — well, two really — came back to bite Sirianni. That's two straight weeks now where the Eagles were in a dominant position to win each game and ended up losing both.

2. Commanders blew OT, but so did the Giants

The Commanders botched the end of overtime about as badly as possible. They had the ball, ample time and downs to win the game and Jayden Daniels seemed to have no clue what was going on .

Blame Daniels, blame Dan Quinn — both are fair game.

This was also the rare game where you reasonably could experience equal rancor for how both teams handled their chances to win. The Giants also should have won, despite the Commanders being up 14 with eight minutes left.

Never mind Washington's self-inflicted mistakes, missing an extra point and committing some critical penalties, including one that wiped out a Jameis Winston interception. The Giants had the ball and needed only to set up a game-winning kick attempt.

They were in business with first-and-10 at the Washington 24-yard line in overtime, under the two-minute stoppage and with the Commanders out of timeouts. All they needed to do was run it three times, center the ball where Dominic Zvada wanted it and go home a winner. An ugly winner, no doubt, but better than a loss or tie.

Instead, Cam Skattebo fumbled it — the one thing he couldn't do. The Commanders recovered, moved the ball 53 yards in six plays and should have won, had it not been for Daniels' clock-killing exploits .

When the clock ran out with the game still tied, Skattebo breathed a sigh of relief . He was lucky his fumble didn't end in a Giants loss. It should have been a win.

3. 49ers rookie provides massive play in huge win

The 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seahawks featured 12 scoring drives, but it really was a defensive grinder for most of it. There was no bigger play in that regard than right before halftime.

The 49ers took an early edge, but the Seahawks started shifting things back in their favor, perhaps inspired by the ejection of the 49ers' Dre Greenlaw . After cutting the 49ers' lead to 14-13, the Seahawks forced a punt, which was downed at the Seattle 1-yard line.

That backed the Seahawks up in the final 20 seconds of the half, and they couldn't simply bleed out the clock because the 49ers had all three timeouts left. On the first play, disaster struck for the home team: 49ers defensive tackle Gracen Halton stripped Seahawks running back George Holani in the end zone and recovered the fumble for a touchdown.

That made it 21-13, San Francisco, at the half. The Seahawks were getting the ball back to start the third quarter, but instead of being able to take the lead, the best they could have done was tie the game.

Granted, there were three second-half lead changes after that point. But the 49ers needed every score they could get on the road, and that one possession was a massive swing at a critical time when the winds had been shifting Seattle's direction.

The rookie Halton had a massive game, also adding a sack, two big run stuffs and a pressure on Sam Darnold's fourth-down pass to Cooper Kupp that came up inches short of a first down, handing the game over to the 49ers.

4. Browns miss multiple chances to beat Jets

The Cleveland Browns had been one of the league's better stories, hitting a 3-1 mark through the first month of the season, but they gave away Sunday's game at the Jets . Even though momentum had shifted in the Browns' favor in the fourth quarter, they could never take advantage of the chances they had.

It all started in the fourth quarter. On the first play of the fourth, Browns rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren intercepted Geno Smith on third down, but Maliek Collins jumped offsides, negating the interception and moving the Jets into field-goal range. Jason Sanders made the 54-yarder to push Cleveland's deficit to 10-6.

Just over 30 game seconds later, the Browns were back in business in Jets territory after Isaiah Bond's 30-yard catch. What followed: illegal formation penalty, sack, delay of game, then another sack. It moved the ball from the New York 45-yard line to the Cleveland 27. The Browns punted on fourth-and-38.

The Jets did the Browns a favor by punting on fourth-and-1 with 10-plus minutes left, and Cleveland moved down the field for the go-ahead score after trailing most of the game. The missed extra point didn't help, but it wasn't the Browns' most fateful mistake.

Smith's lost fumble at his own 43-yard line with 4:20 left was a huge gift, but the Browns couldn't do anything with the ball, using only 19 seconds of clock. On fourth-and-10, the Jets punted — or attempted to. The rain-soaked snap sailed over Corey Bojorquez's head, and the Jets scored a TD three plays later to take the lead.

The Browns had two possessions in the final 3:01 of the game but could do nothing with either. That fateful sequence with the missed PAT and botched snap helped turn a potential Browns edge into a Jets win in the rain.

5. Chargers' biggest blow came before Herbert's late turnovers

The Chargers fell to 0-5, but they had real designs on their first victory of the season. Once again, Justin Herbert's fourth-quarter turnovers — his fifth and sixth of the season — were at the center of the narrative.

But the roots of the Chargers' 23-17 loss to the Broncos can also be traced back one possession earlier.

The Chargers took their first lead late in the third quarter on Kimani Vidal's 42-yard TD run, which came immediately after Tuli Tuipulotu had forced and recovered a Bo Nix fumble. The Broncos had looked stagnant offensively most of the game, even with Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties.

The teams traded punts, as the Chargers' defense stood tall all game, and when Wil Lutz missed a 42-yard field-goal try, it felt like it might be L.A.'s day. But Herbert and the offense couldn't do enough to help pull off the win.

The Chargers lost their little ripple of offensive mojo and stalled at the worst time. Herbert scrambled on third-and-9, and he was marked just short of the line to gain at their own 41-yard line — about the length of the football. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel called for a QB sneak, and Herbert has been very effective on those in his career, but he was stood up immediately and stopped short.

That started the avalanche that followed: a Broncos touchdown and two Herbert turnovers, both of which led to field goals. You can't blame LA's defense for that. The Chargers' offensive miscues flipped a 17-10 Chargers lead into 13 unanswered points and a 23-17 loss .

Herbert's failed sneak opened the door for the Broncos to pull off the comeback. Had the Chargers converted and drained more clock — while resting an exhausted defense a bit more — and perhaps even put up some points, it would have been a different ending. Cameron Dicker still has big range, and the Chargers needed about 20 yards to have given him a shot.

Instead, they turned it over on downs, which was as big and perhaps bigger than the later mistakes.

articles.summary: Kirk Cousins and his family appear to be settling comfortably into life in Nevada.
articles.body: Kirk Cousins and his family appear to be settling comfortably into life in Nevada. His wife, Julie, offered a glimpse of their first weeks in Las Vegas through a social media post ahead of the Raiders’ game against the Buffalo Bills. Her message was short, but it made their feelings about the move clear. “First two months in Nevada… thriving in the desert!” Julie wrote on Instagram. The post also featured family moments from around the city, including a Backstreet Boys concert and scenes of the couple enjoying their new surroundings. For a quarterback adjusting to another NFL team, having his family settle in can make the transition easier.Julie Cousins shares a positive message about life in NevadaJulie’s post offered more than a routine update about the family’s location. It gave Raiders fans a look at how the Cousins family has spent its first two months in Nevada.The photos and videos showed the couple enjoying Las Vegas, a city known for its entertainment options and busy social scene. One clip featured them at a Backstreet Boys concert, taking advantage of the group’s residency in the city. Other footage showed the family exploring their surroundings and supporting Kirk at Raiders games.Julie also shared moments of Kirk spending time with their sons, Cooper and Turner. In one clip, the quarterback tossed a football with the boys, offering a familiar family scene away from the pressure of the NFL.The post arrived as Cousins continued his latest chapter in professional football. The Raiders are his fourth NFL franchise, making another move a significant change for the quarterback and his family. Julie has been part of his journey since before their marriage in 2014, and the family has experienced the demands that come with his career.Her message suggests that the adjustment to Nevada has been going well so far. While one social media post cannot tell the full story of a family’s move, the images offered a positive public snapshot of their new life.Raiders fans welcome Kirk Cousins and his familyJulie’s message also gave Raiders supporters a chance to welcome the family. He sets such a great example and we are thrilled he's having a great season with the Raiders."Another fan welcomed the family with a simple message: "Welcome to Las Vegas. articles.title: Who is Jaime Taylor? Inside Lamar Jackson’s private love story with his longtime girlfriend away from the NFL spotlight
articles.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has two MVP awards and a spot among the NFL's most watched players, yet the person closest to him barely exists online.
articles.body: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has two MVP awards and a spot among the NFL's most watched players, yet the person closest to him barely exists online. Jaime Taylor, his girlfriend of many years and the mother of his daughter, has no public social media account and rarely appears at games or red carpet events. The two met at a Florida high school long before football made him famous. Their story stands out in a league where partners often build their own followings, and the couple seems perfectly happy to keep it that way.Who is Jaime Taylor, Lamar Jackson's longtime girlfriend?Jaime Taylor has built her life away from the cameras. She has no public social media account, and no confirmed photos of her circulate widely. One outlet reports she works in the beauty industry, but that detail has not been verified.What is on record is the family she shares with Jackson. Their daughter, Milan, was born on January 4, 2021. Jackson occasionally posts a light moment with her, once using her nickname, Lani, but he rarely shares more than that. Even a quarterback with his profile keeps home life off the timeline.How did Lamar Jackson and Jaime Taylor meet?The story starts in Florida. According to Heavy, Jackson and Taylor met around 2014 at Boynton Beach Community High School.They began dating while he played at the University of Louisville, as Sporting News has reported. He won the Heisman Trophy there in 2016, and the Ravens picked him 32nd overall in 2018. His first MVP followed in 2019, with a second in 2023. Taylor was there for every step of that climb, yet she never turned it into a public role. The relationship also predates the fame, which could be why she has never felt a need to chase any of it.What has Jaime Taylor said about life with Lamar Jackson?Taylor has spoken publicly only once that is widely known. In a 2019 interview with the Ravens' media team, she explained how Jackson shaped the way she handles outside noise."He's taught me how to handle criticism," she said. "I used to get mad when I'd read stuff. Then I'd look at him, and he's just fine. He says, 'Let them do the talking. You don't have to say anything. Just show them.'"She added that his calm rubs off on her too. "He never lets outside noise define him. That's something I've learned from him every day."It is a small window, but it shows the quiet is a shared approach, not an accident.Why does Jaime Taylor stay out of the spotlight?A Ravens insider once told Baltimore Beatdown that she is a steadying presence. "She's his calm," the insider said. "He's a competitor, but she gives him balance."That fits how the couple operates. Taylor rarely joins Jackson at events, and he keeps his own posts focused on football. Privacy here looks like a decision, and it appears to work for them. Jackson answers for his play every Sunday, while his home is the one place nobody gets to grade.For now, the only glimpses fans get come from Jackson himself, usually when Milan is involved.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tom Brady, the New England Patriots’ legend, went through a tough time in 2022 as he announced his divorce with ex wife, Gisele Bundchen, while he was
articles.body: Tom Brady, the New England Patriots’ legend, went through a tough time in 2022 as he announced his divorce with ex wife, Gisele Bundchen, while he was actively playing in the league. At a time when more and more revelations about their divorce have been released by Tom Brady’s autobiographer, the NFL legend’s comments on dealing with have resurfaced.Tom Brady’s comments about dealing with his divorce resurface as more revelations are releasedIn 2022, just days after announcing his divorce, the seven time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady made an appearance on a podcast where he said, "I think there's a lot of professionals in life that go through things that they deal with at work and they deal with at home…Obviously, the good news is it's a very amicable situation and I'm really focused on two things, taking care of my family and certainly my children, and secondly, doing the best job I can to win football games.”The New England Patriots’ legend added, "So, that's what professionals do. You focus at work when it's time to work, and then when you come home you focus on the priorities that are at home. All you can do is the best you could do. That's what I'll just continue to do as long as I'm working and as long as I'm being a dad…”Tom Brady continued, "I have incredible parents that have always taught me the right way to do things. I want to be a great father to my children and always try to do things the right way as well," Brady continued. "And to deal with things in your life that have challenges, you wanna deal with them in the best possible way. So, I want to always be able to hold my head high on and off the field, and I'm gonna try to continue to do that for as long as I'm here."Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen had a perfect marriage before things ended in 2022Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen’s divorce have continued to dominate headlines for years even as the Brazilian supermodel has moved on in her life, remarried for a second time and also had another son.There have been a lot of speculations about their separation as many have blamed Tom Brady’s commitment to his career being the primary reason behind his divorce.However, none of the controversies have been proven true as Tom Brady and his ex wife have tried to keep themselves away from the mess and focus on raising their children and being there for them.The NFL legend has since stayed single as his primary focus has been his family and work as he spends time with his children.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: George Kittle’s Mike Evans admiration spills onto social media with 6-word post
articles.summary: George Kittle should work in a donut shop. Because he sure knows how to glaze. Mike Evans helped the San Francisco 49ers survive the Seattle Seahawks, 32-29...
articles.body:
George Kittle should work in a donut shop. Because he sure knows how to glaze.

Mike Evans helped the San Francisco 49ers survive the Seattle Seahawks, 32-29, at Lumen Field on Sunday and remain unbeaten in five games. He was on point in their final drives, repeatedly connecting with Brock Purdy to move the ball, leading to the game-winning 43-yard field goal by Eddy Pineiro.

The 33-year-old Evans had seven receptions for 113 yards and one touchdown, and Kittle did not need any hyperbole to express his admiration for the veteran pass-catcher.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Mike Evans is really good at football," said the 33-year-old Kittle on X.

An astute observation, if ever there was one. Who needs advanced analytics, right?

"Mike Evans is a dream come true," said @nineralex.

"I think George is on to something here 😆🤩," added @tonyuncleAL19.

"Like really, really good," wrote @Killahkali7o7.

"Scientists just identified his catch radius as a ring of Saturn," posted @Sublimator2000.

"He picked up the team on his back 😊👍🏽," commented @CitusViratus.

Kittle, for his part, had five receptions for 24 yards.

Purdy went 19-of-29 for 189 yards and two touchdowns. He also heaped praise on Evans, calling the six-time Pro Bowler a "game-changer" and a "true X receiver," as reported by the Associated Press' Josh Dubow.

Evans, who is dealing with a rib injury , has shown that the 49ers made the right decision in prying him away from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with a three-year, $42.4 million contract in the offseason.

The 49ers have a 5-o start for the second time in four years. In 2023, they went all the way to the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Kyle Hamilton Injury Update: Ravens All-Pro Briefly Leaves Game Against Falcons
articles.summary: Ravens All-Pro Kyle Hamilton had to leave Sunday's Week 5 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The post Kyle Hamilton Injury Update: Ravens All-Pro Briefly Leav...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have a once-in-a-generation talent in NFL All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton — a player they can ill afford to lose after he was hurt against the Atlanta Falcons in Sunday's Week 5 game.

"Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton is running off to the sideline after being looked at by trainers," ESPN's Jamison Hensley wrote on his official X account. "He's headed to the sideline medical tent."

Hamilton's time off the field was brief — he returned to the game on a 4th & 2 for the Falcons, with the Ravens trailing 17-15 in the 3rd quarter.

"Kyle Hamilton trying to get back in the game on 4th-and-2," The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec wrote on his official X account. "He did."

Ravens Broke Bank for Kyle Hamilton in 2025

Hamilton and the Ravens agreed to a massive, $100.4 million contract extension in August 2025 that made him the highest-paid safety in NFL history and keeps the 2-time NFL All-Pro with the team through 2029.

The deal also includes another record-setting number: $82 million in guaranteed money.

"All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and the Baltimore Ravens reached agreement today on a four-year, $100.4 million extension, the largest for a safety in NFL history," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on August 27. "The deal … includes $82 million guaranteed — which surpasses the previous record of $45M for a Safety."

Hamilton, who is only 25 years old, was in the final season of the 4-year, $16.25 million contract he signed with the Ravens after they selected him in the first round (No. 14 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft.

Relief After Kyle Hamilton Returns to Game

If there is one defender the Ravens couldn't stand to lose, it's Hamilton.

ESPN's Bill Barnwell picked Hamilton, perhaps the NFL's most versatile defensive player, as one of the 2 safeties on his 2025 NFL All-Pro Team alongside Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James .

"Hamilton's versatility has been essential for the Ravens," Barnwell wrote. "Last year, the Ravens salvaged what had been a frustrating defense by moving Hamilton into a deep-lying role, and they fielded one of the best defenses in the NFL from that point forward. This year? With the defense struggling to start the season, coordinator Zach Orr moved Hamilton back into the box, where he has had a James-like impact around the line of scrimmage. You're not really supposed to be able to play both of those roles at an All-Pro level. Hamilton does."

articles.title: Heat rookie cites a specific aspect that he’s looking to take from Klay Thompson
articles.summary: MIAMI – As the Miami Heat will be led by the dynamic duo of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, there will also be young players who will look to make an...
articles.body:
MIAMI – As the Miami Heat will be led by the dynamic duo of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, there will also be young players who will look to make an immediate impact, such as rookie Ryan Conwell. While the Heat rookie has already been shouted out by the likes of Klay Thompson , the second-round pick would reveal what he has taken away from the four-time champion with the Golden State Warriors.

In Miami's 125-124 preseason loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Conwell would get an extended role with the team as the projected starters of Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Thompson, Andrew Wiggins, and Davion Mitchell didn't play. Along with some of the rotational players being absent, Conwell showed many traits, including his three-point ability that was present in college.

Heat's Ryan Conwell on what he's seen Klay Thompson do all the time

Selected with the 37th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, the Heat took Conwell, who recorded a year each with a different school such as USF, Indiana State, Xavier, and Louisville. The three-point ability was really showcased starting with Indiana State, as he shot over 40 percent from deep with the Sycamores and Xavier, and while it dipped to 34.5 percent with the Cardinals, he attempted 9.6 three-point shots per game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In Saturday's preseason contest, Conwell would log a game-high 22 points on seven of 18 shooting from the field, two of nine from deep, six of seven from the free-throw line, to go along with nine assists, five rebounds, and two steals.

On Saturday, Miami's coaching staff ran a ton of plays with Conwell shooting motion threes off an inbound pass, which the team wants him to do more of, as it helps; he's seen Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. do it many times.

"Yeah, they definitely are," Conwell said when asked if the team is pushing him to take those types of shots. "They pour a lot of confidence into me every day, and I get a lot of confidence from the work I put in in the gym with the other coaches as well. Also, I mean, I watch Klay and Tim do it all the time, so I'm just learning every day, and yeah, just putting in the work."

Despite the two-of-nine clip from deep, there's no denying that the team and Conwell aren't worried about his sharpshooter mentality.

Heat's Erik Spoelstra on Ryan Conwell overcoming the "ups and downs"

Conwell's three-point ability has been hyped ever since he was taken by the Heat in the 2026 NBA Draft, with Thompson himself saying during training camp that the rookie beat him in a shooting drill. However, Saturday's outing showcased Conwell's playmaking ability, as the 22-year-old has been tasked with learning to initiate the offense for Miami, especially since the point-guard depth has been hit with Dru Smith's calf injury.

While the nine assists are encouraging, head coach Erik Spoelstra would tell ClutchPoints that he's overcoming the "ups and downs" he's had in training camp, further explaining the trust he had in the guard during the preseason loss.

"Well, he showed the fortitude to stick with it. He's had some ups and downs in training camp, welcome to the league as a young player, but we feel he has the makeup to be able to weather all these things that will continue to happen when you're a young player. You can see what he's made of," Spoelstra said.

"He made some big plays in the second half as he got settled into the game; you can feel his competitive spirit on both ends of the court, and made some really nice plays," Spoelstra continued. "Obviously, had a couple threes that were big, but he made some plays off the dribble, and we were running, you know, some of the triggers in the fourth quarter, really, for him to make the read, whether it was a shot or get us into something, and he did a nice job with it."

Heat's Ryan Conwell on the game slowing down for him

While Conwell wouldn't connect on what could've been the game-winning shot with time expiring in the fourth quarter, the performance overall shouldn't be undervalued. His words shouldn't be undersold as well, as he told ClutchPoints after the game that aside from gaining more comfortability with the team, "the game is slowing down each day."

"First and foremost, want to give all glory to God. I'm just blessed to be in this position, part of a great organization," Conwell said. "But credit to my coaching staff and to my vets. You know, every day in practice, I'm able just to work on my reads, work on different things, different pieces of my game, and I think with each day, it's showing out there on the floor. It's getting more and more comfortable. The game is slowing down each day, so it's just a work in progress, and I'm just trying to get better at it every single day, just to be an all-around player."

At any rate, it remains to be seen how Conwell's role will be with Miami come the regular-season opener on Oct. 21 against the Minnesota Timberwolves, but he'll continue fine-tuning his skills in the upcoming preseason contest on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets.
